Subject: Need help reconciling account routing for Acme — urgent ahead of Q3

Hi Kimberly / Jonas,

Hope you’re both well. We’re preparing our Q3 co-sell plan and discovered conflicting ownership flags for several Acme corporate accounts. Current overlap is causing duplicate outreach from our partners and impacting deal motion. Can Redwood validate the canonical owner and provide a reconciled account map?

Attached is a short routing summary from our side (Acme_Routing_Summary.pdf) — it calls out 18 accounts with overlapping claims between your channel partners and a subset of your direct field teams. Primary asks:
- Can you confirm which Redwood partner(s) are co-sell enabled for each account?
- We need a single point of contact for legal/contract sign-off per account for procurement timelines.
- Is there a recommended arbitration route if two partners both claim the same named account?

We’re under a procurement deadline on 6/15 so any timeline you can share would be helpful.

Thanks,
Jess Harper
Head of Strategic Alliances
Acme Analytics

Jess — thanks for the note and the summary. We can absolutely help. High level plan below; I’ve attached a working worksheet (AccountMap_Q2_v3.xlsx) to start the reconciliation.

Proposed cadence:
- Today (Wed): quick sync to agree fields and precedence rules (15–20 min).
- Wed-Fri: Redwood + Acme match on authoritative account IDs and determine partner flags.
- Mon 6/7: deliver reconciled worksheet and proposed routing policy; request sign-off by 6/10.

Precedence suggestions (we’ll formalize in the worksheet):
1) Existing ARR with partner-managed contract (highest precedence)
2) Active joint opportunity with documented co-sell engagement (deal stage >= PO)
3) Historical partner ownership (last 12 months activity)
4) Field-owner override (requires regional sales leader approval)

Open items for the quick sync:
- Which HubSpot account id is canonical for Acme (we prefer HubSpot but will accept CRM id mapping).
- Any internal partner NDAs that restrict sharing of pipeline-level info.
- Contact for procurement lane at Acme for final sign-off.

I’m looping in Jonas and Marissa — Jonas will propose the precedence rules as a short algorithm and Marissa will follow-up on partner notifications and escalation if required.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Alliances Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks — adding the suggested precedence as a compact decision tree we can run programmatically against the sheet. Quick proposal (will codify in Claim_Precedence_Rules.docx):
- If partner has a signed SOW or active reserved capacity agreement that references the account -> assign to partner.
- Else if opportunity exists in HubSpot with partner role flagged and stage >= Proposal -> co-owned; create a joint-owner tag and route communications through partner/field pairing.
- Else if partner activity in last 90 days (meetings/logged touches) > field touches -> prefer partner but notify field for concurrence.
- Otherwise default to field owner with CC to partner.

I pushed a sanitized sample mapping to the HubSpot deal noted below for your reference so Acme can cross-check ids: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345/DEAL-ACME-4721

If we get Acme sign-off on the precedence table by end of day Tue 6/8 we can run the reconciliation and produce an authoritative map by 6/10.

Jonas Weber
